chunks: Al-Fadl, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Qaim will not reappear except in an odd number of years: nine, three, five, and one.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser, a title for Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) referring to his reappearance
key_terms.وَتْرٍ: Odd number (singular of awtar), referring to years ending in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9

ai.seo_question: What type of year will Imam Mahdi's reappearance occur in according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), the term 'Witr' (odd) signifies that the reappearance will occur in a year with an odd number, specifically highlighting one, three, five, and nine as key possibilities. This aligns with the broader Shia eschatological tradition which emphasizes the unpredictability of the exact timing while providing numerical signs for the discerning believer. The specificity of these numbers reflects the scholarly interpretation of 'Witr' not just as a general oddity, but as a distinct marker within the cycle of years preceding the global justice of the Qaim.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 460 - Fadhl has narrated from Ibn Mahbub from Ali bin Abi Hamza from Abu Basir from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that he said:
The Qaim will not reappear, except in an odd year, like 9, 3, 5 and 1.
